outputs.L3:
A printed circuit board comprises at least one insulating layer and at least one conducting layer arranged on or in relation to the insulating layer. The conducting layer is structured to form a contact surface intended for electrical and mechanical connection to an electronic component, such as a semiconductor component, power device, or other heat-generating electronic element.

In the region of the contact surface, at least one channel extends through the contact surface and through the insulating layer. The channel may be formed as a bore, via, recess, or other through-opening. It is positioned so that it passes through the area used for mounting or contacting the electronic component. To improve thermal performance, the channel is filled with, or at least lined with, a thermally conductive material. This material provides an efficient heat-conducting path from the electronic component, through the contact surface and insulating layer, to another region of the printed circuit board or to a heat-dissipating structure. As a result, heat generated during operation of the electronic component can be transferred away more effectively, improving reliability and reducing thermal stress.

A corresponding manufacturing process includes first providing a printed circuit board substrate having an insulating layer and a conducting layer. At least one channel is then produced in the region of the future contact surface, for example by drilling, laser processing, etching, punching, or another suitable material-removal process. The channel is subsequently filled or lined with a thermally conductive material, such as copper or another metal, a thermally conductive paste, or a thermally conductive composite. The conducting layer is then structured to form the contact surface for the electronic component. Depending on the process sequence, the structuring of the conducting layer may also take place before or partly during the formation or lining of the channel.

After the contact surface has been formed, a solder deposit is applied to it. The solder deposit may be provided as solder paste, a solder preform, or another suitable solder material. The electronic component is then placed onto the contact surface so that its corresponding terminal or mounting surface is aligned with the solder deposit. The solder is subsequently melted, for example by reflow soldering, wave soldering, selective soldering, or another thermal joining process. During melting, the solder forms a mechanical and electrical connection between the electronic component and the contact surface. Finally, the assembly is cooled, causing the solder to solidify and secure the component in place.

Through the thermally conductive material in the channel, the printed circuit board provides enhanced heat dissipation directly beneath or near the contact surface of the mounted electronic component. This configuration is particularly advantageous for components that generate significant heat, since it improves thermal transfer while maintaining the electrical connection and mechanical support provided by the structured conducting layer.
outputs.L4:
A printed circuit board design and manufacturing method are provided to improve heat dissipation from an electronic component mounted on the board. In this design, one or more thermally conductive channels are formed through a component contact surface and an underlying insulating layer of the printed circuit board. These channels create direct or enhanced thermal pathways that allow heat generated by the electronic component to be transferred away from the mounting area more efficiently than in a conventional board structure.

The thermally conductive channels may be filled, plated, or otherwise provided with a material having high thermal conductivity, such as copper or another suitable metal. When the electronic component is attached to the contact surface, heat produced during operation is conducted through the contact region and into the channels. From there, the heat may be distributed into internal conductive layers, a heat-spreading region, a thermal pad, or another heat-dissipating structure associated with the printed circuit board.

The manufacturing method may include forming an insulating layer on or within the printed circuit board, defining a component contact surface, creating openings or vias through the contact surface and insulating layer, and filling or lining those openings with thermally conductive material. The conductive channels are positioned to correspond to high-heat regions of the mounted component, thereby improving the efficiency of heat transfer while maintaining the required electrical insulation and mechanical support of the board.

By providing thermally conductive channels through the contact surface and insulating layer, the resulting printed circuit board structure reduces thermal resistance between the electronic component and the board. This improved thermal conduction helps lower the operating temperature of the component, reduces the risk of overheating, and enhances the long-term reliability and performance of the assembled electronic device.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest words in the English language, yet it plays a very important role. It is called the definite article, and it helps us talk about something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean a particular book that the listener or reader can identify.

This simple word brings clarity to communication. It points to people, places, objects, and ideas that are already known or understood. Phrases like “the sun,” “the world,” and “the truth” feel familiar because “the” gives them a sense of importance and certainty.

Although it is short, “the” appears constantly in English writing and speech. It connects sentences smoothly and helps make meaning precise. Without it, language would feel less natural and more confusing.

In many ways, “the” proves that even the smallest words can have a big impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a printed circuit board with thermal vias through a component contact pad, including both the device structure and manufacturing process steps.
counterfactuals.output:
A printed circuit board includes an electrically insulating substrate having a first surface, an opposed second surface, and one or more conductive layers. A component contact pad is disposed on the first surface and is configured to receive a terminal or thermal interface of an electronic component. A plurality of thermal vias extend through the component contact pad and at least partially through the substrate to provide a thermal conduction path from the component contact pad to an internal or external heat-spreading conductor. Each thermal via includes a plated conductive wall and may be filled, capped, or planarized with a thermally conductive material so that an exposed mounting surface of the component contact pad remains substantially coplanar for component attachment.

A method of manufacturing the printed circuit board includes forming or providing the insulating substrate, defining via openings through a region corresponding to the component contact pad, depositing conductive material on walls of the via openings to form plated thermal vias, optionally filling the thermal vias with conductive or thermally conductive fill material, planarizing or capping the filled vias, and forming the component contact pad over and around the thermal vias. The method may further include forming one or more heat-spreading layers coupled to the thermal vias, applying a solder mask with an opening exposing the component contact pad, and mounting an electronic component to the pad such that heat generated by the component is conducted through the thermal vias away from the component contact region.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in formal patent language, a printed circuit board having an insulating substrate, a structured conductive contact pad, and at least one thermally conductive filled channel, plus the steps for producing and populating it.
counterfactuals.output:
A printed circuit board is provided comprising an electrically insulating substrate, at least one structured electrically conductive contact pad arranged on a surface of the substrate, and at least one thermally conductive filled channel extending at least partially through the substrate and being thermally coupled to the structured electrically conductive contact pad.

In one embodiment, the insulating substrate comprises a dielectric base material, for example a fiber-reinforced resin material, ceramic-filled resin, polyimide, epoxy laminate, FR-4 material, or another electrically insulating carrier suitable for printed circuit board manufacture. The structured conductive contact pad is formed from a metal layer, preferably copper or a copper alloy, and is patterned to define a component mounting region. The contact pad may comprise a solderable surface finish, such as nickel/gold, immersion silver, immersion tin, organic solderability preservative, or another metallization suitable for electrical and mechanical connection to an electronic component.

The at least one thermally conductive filled channel is provided in thermal communication with the contact pad. The channel may extend from the contact pad into the substrate, through the substrate, or between opposing surfaces of the substrate. The channel is filled with a thermally conductive filling material, which may comprise copper, silver, aluminum, solder, a conductive paste, a metal-filled polymer, graphite-containing material, ceramic-filled polymer, or another material having a thermal conductivity greater than that of the surrounding insulating substrate. In a preferred embodiment, the filled channel forms a thermal via or thermal plug arranged beneath or adjacent to the structured contact pad so as to conduct heat away from an electronic component mounted on the contact pad.

The structured conductive contact pad may include one or more openings, recesses, slots, bridges, webs, solder-flow control regions, solder-mask-defined regions, or metal-defined regions. The structured configuration may be selected to promote solder wetting, to reduce void formation, to control solder thickness, to improve mechanical anchoring, or to enhance heat transfer to the thermally conductive filled channel. In certain embodiments, a plurality of filled channels is distributed beneath the contact pad in an array, and the contact pad is structured such that the channels are at least partially exposed, covered, or surrounded by conductive pad regions.

A method for producing such a printed circuit board comprises providing an electrically insulating substrate; forming at least one channel in the substrate at a position corresponding to a thermal transfer region of a component contact area; filling the channel with a thermally conductive material; applying or providing an electrically conductive layer on at least one surface of the substrate; and structuring the conductive layer to form at least one conductive contact pad thermally coupled to the filled channel.

The channel may be formed by mechanical drilling, laser drilling, punching, milling, etching, or another subtractive process. The channel may be formed as a blind hole, through-hole, trench, recess, or via opening. Filling of the channel may be carried out by electroplating, electroless plating, screen printing, stencil printing, dispensing, vacuum filling, pressure filling, solder filling, paste insertion, lamination of a conductive plug, or any combination thereof. The filled channel may subsequently be planarized, for example by grinding, polishing, brushing, etching, or chemical-mechanical treatment, to provide a surface substantially flush with the substrate or conductive layer.

In one embodiment, the conductive contact pad is formed by laminating a copper foil to the substrate and subsequently patterning the copper foil by photolithographic masking and etching. In another embodiment, the conductive pad is formed by additive or semi-additive metallization. The structuring of the pad may be performed before or after filling of the channel, provided that the resulting contact pad remains thermally coupled to the filled channel. A solder mask may be applied to the substrate and patterned to expose at least a portion of the contact pad.

A method for populating the printed circuit board comprises applying a bonding material to the structured conductive contact pad, placing an electronic component onto the bonding material such that a terminal, heat slug, thermal pad, electrode, or package underside of the electronic component is aligned with the structured conductive contact pad, and forming a permanent electrical and/or thermal connection between the electronic component and the contact pad. The bonding material may comprise solder paste, sinter paste, conductive adhesive, thermally conductive adhesive, solder preform, or another attachment medium. The connection may be formed by reflow soldering, vapor-phase soldering, wave soldering, selective soldering, thermocompression bonding, sintering, curing, or another joining process.

When the electronic component is mounted, heat generated by the electronic component is conducted from the component through the structured conductive contact pad into the at least one thermally conductive filled channel and from there into the substrate, to an opposite conductive layer, to a heat spreader, or to an external heat sink. The arrangement thereby provides improved thermal dissipation while maintaining electrical insulation in regions of the substrate surrounding the filled channel.

In a further embodiment, the printed circuit board comprises a plurality of conductive layers separated by insulating layers, wherein the thermally conductive filled channel extends through one or more of the insulating layers and is thermally connected to at least one internal or external conductive plane. The conductive plane may serve as a heat spreading layer, ground plane, power plane, or thermally active layer. The filled channel may be electrically connected to the contact pad or may be electrically insulated therefrom by an intervening dielectric or thermally conductive electrically insulating layer, depending on the intended circuit function.

The invention further relates to a printed circuit board assembly comprising the printed circuit board and at least one electronic component mounted on the structured conductive contact pad, wherein the at least one thermally conductive filled channel is arranged to dissipate heat generated by the electronic component during operation. The electronic component may be a power semiconductor, light-emitting diode, processor, voltage regulator, radio-frequency device, sensor, integrated circuit, or other heat-generating component.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a technical summary of a PCB invention where thermal conduction is improved by forming channels through the conductive layer and insulating layer, filling them with heat-conductive material, applying solder, placing a component, melting, and cooling.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention relates to a printed circuit board (PCB) structure and manufacturing method for improving thermal conduction from an electronic component to the board.

A conductive layer, such as a copper circuit layer, is formed on or over an insulating substrate layer. To enhance heat transfer, one or more channels, vias, or openings are formed through both the conductive layer and the insulating layer in a region intended to receive a heat-generating electronic component. These channels are then filled with a thermally conductive material, such as metal, solder-compatible conductive filler, or another high thermal conductivity compound, thereby creating heat-transfer paths through the PCB stack.

After the channels are filled, solder is applied to the conductive layer at the component mounting location. The electronic component is placed onto the solder so that its thermal or electrical contact region aligns with the enhanced thermal conduction area. The assembly is then heated to melt or reflow the solder, allowing the solder to bond the component to the conductive layer and, where applicable, to interface with the thermally conductive filled channels. Upon cooling, the solder solidifies, securing the component and establishing a thermally efficient connection.

The resulting PCB provides improved dissipation of heat generated by the mounted component by conducting heat away through the filled channels and into the board or an associated heat-spreading structure. This approach can reduce component operating temperature, improve reliability, and support higher power density in electronic assemblies.
